decisionRule: Choose the single next implementation concept that improves the most important real workflow while preserving the existing architecture and documented RF/persistence semantics.

options.label: Concept 7G — Results, Lineage & Stale-State UX
whySupported: Wrong-lineage report/apply and stale-result interpretation are the two highest-severity workflow risks.
Existing Scenario, Version, Run, and Report relationships already provide the data needed for clearer context.
The risk spans Plan, Simulate, Analyze, Review, map inspection, optimization, and report generation.
It can be implemented within the current map-first shell without changing RF, optimizer, persistence, or API behavior.
scope: Persistent compact Project / Scenario / Version identity.
Explicit Current, Result out of date, Historical, Unavailable, and Unsupported labels.
Source Run/Version summary on Results, Run History, and Report transitions.
successSignals: A user can name the active Project, Scenario, Version, and current/historical Run without opening a second panel.
After an RF-affecting edit, the UI says which result is out of date and offers a safe next action.
A historical Run or Report remains visibly historical after returning to the map.
Applying a solution or generating a Report shows its source and destination context before commit.
No RF outputs, persistence semantics, or API contracts change.

options.label: Concept 7G — RF Configuration Progressive Disclosure
whySupported: Propagation and RF Diagnostics mix ordinary planning controls with reference/research cards.
Data combines dataset, model, measurement, and calibration responsibilities.
options.riskIfFirst: Without a shared current/historical/Version vocabulary, collapsed panels may reduce visibility without resolving wrong-state risk.

options.label: Concept 7G — Review and Workspace IA Refinement
whySupported: Results, Run history, Data, Report, and Scenario revision detail each own adjacent parts of review.
Report and Run entry points are valid but fragmented.
scope: Reduce artifact terminology in ordinary Reports.
Keep the map and four-stage rail.
options.riskIfFirst: Review IA would be redesigned around an unstable state vocabulary unless lineage is clarified first.

options.label: Concept 7G — Safe Feature Lazy Loading
whySupported: The production JS chunk is 921.62 kB raw / 252.89 kB gzip and Vite warns above 500 kB.
Rare research, validation, experiment, Core Lab, and report modules are eagerly imported.
scope: Lazy-load report export and retained artifact tooling.
options.riskIfFirst: It improves startup but does not address the highest-severity wrong-lineage workflow; loading boundaries could also expose state-loss bugs.

selected.label: Concept 7G — Results, Lineage & Stale-State UX
selected.reason: It improves the most important real workflow—configure, run, inspect, revise, save, report, revisit—while preserving the current map-first architecture and existing domain/persistence semantics.
implementationOrder: Define and test the shared state/lineage vocabulary.
Expose active Project/Scenario/Version identity in the existing header context.
Attach current/historical/stale source summaries to Results, Run History, Report, and apply flows.
Add safe empty/error transitions and focus/context behavior.
Only then implement research disclosure and code-splitting follow-ups.

implementationGuardrails: Do not change RF computations or request/response contracts.
Do not change optimizer scoring, search policy, or Pareto semantics.
Do not change Scenario/Version/Run/Report storage semantics.
Do not introduce a project dashboard unless later evidence shows a pre-map project triage need.
Do not use color alone for Current, Historical, Stale, Unavailable, or Unsupported.
Keep the map visually central and keep expensive computation explicit.
